title: bhakti: the Chaitanya Charitamrita (selections)
hook: a young renunciant faints in a temple, and a scholar carries him home to teach him
tomorrow: a renunciant asks a governor to teach him. why keep saying 'more'?

segments.voice: Yesterday, bhakti in the Chaitanya Charitamrita's opening: love wanted from both sides. Today the week closes, with the book's first big scene.

A group chat has a familiar move: someone posts a take, and the corrections pile on within seconds. This scene runs the other way. A young renunciant walks into the temple of Jagannatha at Puri, sees the image, and drops to the floor, senseless. People stare. One man steps in: Sarvabhauma, a learned teacher of Vedanta. He has the stranger carried to his own house. The stranger is Chaitanya. And the scholar is about to give him lessons.
screen: `A STRANGER FAINTS IN THE TEMPLE.` → `A SCHOLAR CARRIES HIM HOME.` → `THE LESSONS BEGIN.`

segments.voice: In the Charitamrita's telling, Sarvabhauma is kind, and a little protective. He teaches the young man the Vedanta sutras, day after day, and Chaitanya sits and listens without a word. At last the scholar asks: are you understanding any of this? The answer is gentle and blunt at once. I understand the sutras, Chaitanya says. It's your explanation I can't follow. Their meaning is clear, like the sun; the commentary covers it, like a cloud. Then he gives his own reading, with devotion at the center, and the book says the scholar turned to bhakti. Two notes. This is the Charitamrita's story, told by Chaitanya's followers; Shankara's followers read the same sutras through his commentary, and still do. And look at who listened first. Bhakti here doesn't arrive by winning the first exchange. It waits, then speaks plainly. A fitting close to a week that kept choosing patience: a pace sized to last, gifts given with modesty, a review without fever, a choice handed back, and a love wanted from both sides.
screen: `HE LISTENS FOR DAYS.` · `THE SUN, AND THE CLOUD.` · `THE SCHOLAR TURNS TO BHAKTI.` · then, large: `IT WAITS, THEN SPEAKS PLAINLY.`

segments.voice: Listen to one sound near you: a fan, traffic, a clock, your own breath. Stay with it for the whole sit, without explaining it or answering it. When the mind starts preparing a reply, as minds do, come back to listening.
Bhakti: devotion. In this scene, it listens for days before it says a thing, and then it says it plainly.
Carry this: bhakti, from the Chaitanya Charitamrita, a love that listens first. That's the week.

howItsDone: Gaudiya Vaishnavas tell the story of Sarvabhauma at Puri as a turn from dry learning to devotion; Advaita Vedantins continue to read the sutras through Shankara's commentary.
